verdict.detail: The album first came out in 1972 (Jamaica).

notes.text:
Spelling as on back cover. This would appear to be the first reissue with the revised front cover art - still the silkscreen card cover but now black back cover print. It can with certain confidence be dated to Spring 1978 thanks to a Daddy Kool advertisement in the April issue of UK magazine Black Music (see uploaded image). The copy pictured in this entry was purchased at about the same time.

Already in 1978 the matrices look like sh*t so that every copy pressed have that dirty, not-so-glossy look (and audible crackle) that became more commonplace with the 90's reissues of much Jamaican music. Burning Spear's Rocking Time on the Forward label purchased at the same time (and also listed in the Daddy Kool ad) had considerably heavier vinyl than Studio One Presenting and glossy surfaces, with only small factory damages to the matrice/stamper. It played very well for a Studio One record.
